title: SEAL: A Single-Event Architecture for In-Sensor Visual Localization
problem: Traditional binary-encoded image sensors generate large data volumes that create energy and latency bottlenecks during transfer, storage, and processing for visual localization tasks such as keypoint detection and tracking. Moving these operations off-sensor to a host processor adds significant latency and energy cost.
motivation: In-sensor processing can eliminate redundant data movement, but conventional digital pixel sensor designs lack the compute fabric and coding efficiency to run computer vision primitives locally.
method: SEAL replaces binary pixel encoding with delay-based encoding, where each pixel's brightness is represented as a timing delay—how long a signal takes to arrive encodes the brightness value (analog-to-time conversion). This timing data feeds directly into a processor built into the sensor that performs keypoint detection and tracking using race logic, an ultra-efficient technique where computation is encoded in signal arrival times, using just one wire per variable. Before data leaves the sensor, a quantized frontend processor compresses the timing outputs. By keeping the localization computation on the sensor instead of sending raw pixel data to an external computer, SEAL eliminates both the energy and latency bottleneck of data transfer.
key_novelty: SEAL runs the complete keypoint detection and tracking pipeline inside the pixel sensor using timing-based encoding (race logic) instead of binary encoding, all implemented in fully digital CMOS circuits.
contributions: SEAL architecture: in-sensor temporal processor for keypoint detection and tracking using race logic delay coding.
Co-design of analog-to-time converters with digital temporal processing circuits using standard CMOS/EDA tools.
16-61x latency reduction in keypoint detection and tracking vs. software baselines on host processor.
7x energy reduction vs. standard digital pixel sensor without processing; preserves VIO tracking accuracy (<=1 cm RMSE ATE change on EuRoC).

metrics.speedup: 16-61x latency reduction for keypoint detection and tracking vs. software baseline on host processor
metrics.energy_or_tops_w: 7x energy reduction vs. standard digital pixel sensor
metrics.accuracy: ATE RMSE changes: -1.0 cm (HybVIO), +0.3 cm (VINS-Mono) on EuRoC

baselines: standard digital pixel sensor without in-sensor processing
limitations: Evaluation combines analog/digital simulation and FPGA prototyping but lacks fabricated silicon results; race logic encoding restricts the class of computable operations.
primary_theme: In-sensor visual localization via delay-based race logic encoding
